# Results -- Study 513 (Size-Effect / Banz 1981 SMB) on a real yfinance basket

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: each month-end rank a
fixed ~40-name survivor basket by market capitalisation, long the small half / short the large
half (equal-weight, dollar-neutral and beta-neutral), one execution lag (signal through month
*m*, return realised in month *m+1*), costs + short borrow charged. As-of **2026-06-26**.*

## The verdict, earned -- Signal `NONE` - Tradability `MIRAGE` - "January concentration?" `BUSTED`

Rolf Banz (1981) found that small-cap stocks earned higher risk-adjusted returns than
large-caps -- the original cross-sectional anomaly, later packaged as Fama-French's **SMB**.
On a 40-name survivor basket spanning mega-caps down to genuine small/mid-caps, 2001-2026,
the small-minus-large long-short earns **-1.08%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-0.48** -- not merely
short of the bar, but the *wrong sign*. A label-shuffle placebo puts the real *t* squarely
inside the null (*p* = **0.61**). The small leg trailed the large leg on both return
(+13.3% vs +14.4%/yr) and Sharpe (0.82 vs 1.01) in this mega-cap-led era. The famous
**January** small-cap pop is **absent** here (Januaries were the *worst* month for the
spread, -1.0%/mo, Welch *p* = 0.10). So `NONE` on the signal, `MIRAGE` on tradability
(net of costs the book is -2.1%/yr), and the January-concentration question is `BUSTED` on
this tape.

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Prices (daily adjusted-close) | 6389 days x 40 tickers | `54a77c8e6180` |
| SPY (market proxy) | 6389 days | `5898b297d67e` |
| Caps (current marketCap anchor) | 40 tickers | `17f05782d1ad` |
| Period covered | 2001-01-02 -- 2026-05-29 | -- |

**Source:** yfinance daily adjusted-close (auto_adjust=True) + `.info` marketCap. Basket: 20
large-caps (AAPL ... INTC) and 20 genuine small/mid-caps (SXT, WDFC, JJSF, CASS, STBA, ...);
median-cap split gives a clean 20/20 small/large partition.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is the set of names still trading in
2026, projected backwards. Failed small-caps -- the natural *long* leg of a size trade -- have
been removed, which biases the size premium **upward**. The premium is *still* negative here,
so the true (delisting-included) premium is no better. Caps are reconstructed as
`cap_now * price_t / price_now` (shares-constant approximation -- ignores buybacks/issuance;
adequate for ranking a stable basket but stated as a limitation).

## The honest test -- small-minus-large long-short

One execution lag: caps are known through month-end *m*; the equal-weight long-small /
short-large position is held over month *m+1*. No same-bar fill, no look-ahead.

| Statistic | Dollar-neutral | Beta-neutral |
|---|---|---|
| N months | 304 (2001-02 -- 2026-05) | 304 |
| Mean return (annualised) | **-1.08%/yr** | -1.76%/yr |
| Sharpe (annual) | -0.090 | -0.146 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.483** | -0.755 |
| Hit rate (months > 0) | 43.8% | -- |
| Max drawdown | -57.8% | -- |
| Avg beta-hedge ratio | -- | 0.967 |

- The size premium is **negative and statistically zero**: HAC *t* = -0.48, far inside
  |*t*| >= 2. Hedging out market beta (ratio ~0.97 -- small and large were near-equal beta
  on this basket) does not help; the beta-neutral book is -1.76%/yr.
- The legs explain it: the **large** leg out-earned the **small** leg on both raw return
  (+14.4% vs +13.3%/yr) and Sharpe (1.01 vs 0.82). 2001-2026 was a large-cap decade.

## Placebo -- label-shuffle null

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real dollar-neutral HAC *t* | -0.483 |
| Placebo *p* (share of 300 shuffles with \|t_null\| >= \|t_real\|) | **0.613** |

Shuffling the small/large labels each month and re-running 300 times reproduces a *t* at
least as extreme as the real one **61%** of the time. The real spread is indistinguishable
from random label assignment.

## Costs -- gross vs net

| Book | Mean (ann) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|---|
| Dollar-neutral, **gross** | -1.08%/yr | -0.483 |
| Dollar-neutral, **net** (10 bps x turnover + 100 bps/yr borrow) | **-2.08%/yr** | -0.933 |

Average monthly name-turnover is tiny (~0.4% -- the basket is stable so the median split
rarely moves a name), so trading cost is negligible; the **short borrow** (100 bps/yr on the
ever-present short large-cap leg) does most of the damage, dragging the already-negative
book to -2.1%/yr.

## January concentration (the anomaly's signature) -- BUSTED

| Window | Mean spread | n |
|---|---|---|
| January | **-1.01%/mo** | 25 |
| Other 11 months | -0.01%/mo | 279 |
| Welch *t* / *p* | -1.681 / 0.103 | -- |

Banz's small-cap premium famously concentrated in **January** (the turn-of-year tax-loss /
window-dressing bounce). On this survivor basket the effect is **reversed**: January was the
*worst* month for small-minus-large (-1.0%/mo vs ~0 the rest of the year), and the difference
leans the wrong way (Welch *p* = 0.10). The January-small-cap signature is **busted** here.

## Decay within sample (early vs late)

| Window | Mean (ann) | HAC *t* | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early (2001-2013) | **+1.76%/yr** | +0.556 | 149 |
| Late (2013-2026) | **-3.81%/yr** | -1.245 | 155 |

Consistent with the documented post-publication / post-1980 decay: what little positive size
tilt existed early in the sample (2001-2013, +1.8%/yr but already insignificant) **flipped
negative** in the mega-cap-led 2013-2026 era (-3.8%/yr). Neither half clears the bar; the
trend is the well-known fade.

## Synthetic positive control (faithful-engine check, 25 seeds)

| Run | Mean HAC *t* | frac \|t\|>2 |
|---|---|---|
| Planted 6%/yr small-cap premium | **+2.73** | 0.72 |
| Null (0%) | +0.81 | 0.08 |

With a real premium planted, the **same sort/long-short/HAC pipeline** recovers it (mean
*t* = +2.73 over 25 independent seeds, *t*>2 in 72% of draws); under the null it stays low.
The engine is faithful and powered -- so the flat real-tape result is a property of the
**data**, not a broken harness. *(This control is a power check only; it does not support
the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** SMB earns -1.08%/yr at HAC *t* = -0.48 over 304 months, placebo
  *p* = 0.61. The premium is the wrong sign and statistically zero. Banz (1981) and the
  SMB literature provide a strong prior on a *broad, non-survivor* universe, but on this
  40-name survivor basket -- the large-cap decade of 2001-2026 -- there is no size premium.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Sharpe -0.09 gross, -0.17 net; the short borrow alone makes
  the book lose an extra ~1%/yr. There is nothing to trade.
- **January concentration? -- BUSTED.** The anomaly's signature January pop is absent and
  reversed here.
- **Survivorship -- Named.** Basket = names still trading in 2026; failed small-caps (the
  natural long) are absent, biasing the premium *upward* -- and it is *still* negative.
